name: Lyrion Laurel-Envoy
campaignHooks: Campaign 02: Trial of the Celestial Heights
loreTies: Lyrion designs divine contests to measure whether Deities deserve passage through contested Gates. He frames battles as tests of excellence rather than simple survival.
shortBackstory: Lyrion Laurel-Envoy belongs to The Celestial Heights of Olympus, the older source behind human myth. Lyrion is a laurel-envoy of contest law: part diplomat, part oracle usher, part arena architect. His bronze, marble-light, laurel seals, and measured beauty should feel like the origin of later Greek diplomatic and athletic sacred culture.

chapters.title: Before the Gate Spoke
chapters.text: Lyrion Laurel-Envoy was important before battle records named them. As diplomatic envoy and contest architect, Lyrion Laurel-Envoy learned the hidden machinery beneath The Celestial Heights of Olympus: who records law, who witnesses oath, who warns the living world, and who profits when warnings are ignored.

chapters.title: Faction Duty
chapters.text: Lyrion Laurel-Envoy's loyalty is tied to Olympian culture rather than battlefield glory. Their doctrine is simple and dangerous: Excellence proves divinity. The story needs them because Deities can win fights and still misunderstand what victory costs.

chapters.title: Story Arc Tie
chapters.text: During Storm-Oath Covenant, Lyrion Laurel-Envoy becomes a readable witness to campaign consequence. Their first appearance, Campaign 02: Trial of the Celestial Heights, places them where player decisions need interpretation, warning, and memory instead of another controllable unit.

chapters.title: Conflict Wound
chapters.text: The Gate pressures Lyrion Laurel-Envoy through knowledge. It offers signs that are useful but incomplete, trying to turn witness into accomplice. Their recurring conflict is whether to reveal truth early and risk panic, or wait for proof and risk lives.

chapters.title: Dashboard Role
chapters.text: As a non-playable character, Lyrion Laurel-Envoy belongs under Characters and Character Backstories. Their profile should be read beside campaign dialogue, codex unlocks, and faction pages so every briefing feels like canon consequence, not tutorial flavor.
